llm.summary: This appears to be a real browser collection helper, but it gives the agent broad local execution and credential-handling authority that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The local and cloud collection flows match the stated purpose, but the skill also supports arbitrary bridge startup commands, authenticated local bridge control, stop/reset operations, and cloud dispatch of collection payloads.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill documents local/cloud modes and tokens, but it under-discloses the practical impact of sending payloads and bearer tokens to the cloud backend, using the normal Chrome environment, and accepting shell command strings for bridge startup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No deceptive installer or dependency behavior was found; bundled scripts are explicit shell helpers. The main install-time concern is that normal use can create persistent preferences containing sensitive cloud configuration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local bridge access and cloud API use are proportionate to browser collection, but automatic admin-token discovery and configurable cloud base URLs are broader than necessary without stronger user confirmation or destination controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill can store cloud tokens in a regular JSON preferences file, read a local bridge admin token from the user's home directory, and start a background bridge process through a shell command.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and need this exact local/cloud browser-collection workflow. Prefer local mode when possible, avoid persisting cloud tokens unless you accept plaintext local-file storage, do not let untrusted text control --bridge-cmd or WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD, use a scoped/rotatable API token, and consider a separate Chrome profile for sensitive browsing sessions.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Using a local bridge admin token is related to controlling the connector, but the script auto-discovers it from the environment or a predictable home-directory file and attaches it to bridge requests without a separate opt-in.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Persisting defaultCloudToken and defaultCloudDeviceId supports convenience, but plaintext token storage in the skill preferences file is a sensitive credential-handling concern rather than a necessary collection behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Cloud mode necessarily sends a payload, device ID, and bearer token to the configured backend, but the user-facing instructions do not create a strong consent boundary before external dispatch.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The local bridge startup path executes a user-controlled command string via bash -lc; starting the connector is purpose-related, but arbitrary shell execution is overbroad for a collection helper.
[SQP-2] expected: run.sh forwards collection payloads and bearer credentials to the cloud loop in cloud mode as documented, but it lacks HTTPS enforcement or host allowlisting for overridden cloud endpoints.
